scope: Read-only review of two fixture timing corrections; production source and prior31-file review receipt unchanged.

preserved_failed_source_cuts.diagnosis: The immediate GetTask assertion observed working rather than unknown. The correction waits for the same task to settle without admitting another task/effect.

The acquisition-completion poll observed unauthorised under the original eight-second grant measured before server startup. Moving startup outside a thirty-second real lease retains the original-expiry assertions; the timing diagnosis is an inference from the failure and fixture schedule.

corrections.change: Replace one immediate expected-unknown observation with a bounded thirty-second GetTask poll on the same authorised recovery task ID.
preserved_assertions: HTTP200 and no GetTask error are required while polling.
Only submitted or working may precede the required unknown state; completed, failed and other states fail.
Exactly one recorded external call before restart.
Restart replays the exact original SendMessage, requires an error, and external call count stays one.
Revoked authority hides task/recovery metadata and still cannot cause another external call.
corrections.assessment: The poll accommodates asynchronous settlement without accepting success, arbitrary states, a new task or redispatch.

corrections.change: Start the server before defining the short grant; extend the real admission lease from eight to thirty seconds.
preserved_assertions: Shorten the grant before submitting the actual acquisition.
A positive initial source read is required and source_metadata.expires_at_ms must equal the exact original short expiry.
Wait until wall time exceeds that same original expiry.
Renew only the same-epoch current grant expiry to original_expiry+300000; original source metadata is not rewritten.
Source, task and existing retained-effect delivery methods all deny afterward without a result payload.
Journal content equals its pre-expiry snapshot and exactly one external call is recorded.
corrections.assessment: The thirty-second window remains a real expiry test. Startup no longer consumes the fixture admission lease; no assertion accepts renewed source expiry or redispatch.
corrections.timing_limit: This checks the declared local real-time schedule, not a deployment latency guarantee or immunity to arbitrary clock adjustment/load.
